insight.title: Why Focusing on Less Helps You Move Faster
insight.subtitle: How ignoring the big picture helps you navigate it better

sections.text: A single bird turning at the edge of a flock can change the direction of a thousand others. In nature, starlings navigate massive obstacles by simply tracking the seven neighbors closest to them.

This "rule of seven" allows the flock to react instantly. They don't monitor the entire sky; they just maintain a precise alignment with their immediate surroundings, which ripples through the whole group.
We often stall by trying to control every outcome at once. Real momentum is created by ignoring the big picture and focusing on the small variables within your immediate reach.
Try this today: When you make a difficult decision today, focus only on the next three minutes of impact.
Precision is found by shrinking your world until the next move becomes obvious.
